Capstone: build a web server

Proposed

The Cookbook's version is about 2,400 lines, including its demo and load test. Your core build has ten steps, about 1 to 2 hours each, and every step ends with something you can run and test. Times are estimates.

  1. Read one requestFrom bytes in memory
  2. Handle pieces and limitsHalf a request, several, or too much
  3. Write responsesIncluding ones produced bit by bit
  4. Routes and shared stepsLogging, timing and failure handling
  5. Serve one clientOver a real connection
  6. Serve many clientsWorkers, and a clear reply when full
  7. Keep connections openSeveral requests, with time limits
  8. Serve filesSafely, in parts, and only when changed
  9. Report what is happeningCounts and timings
  10. Shut down cleanlyFinish accepted work, then stop

Optional afterwards: a load test and a comparison with an async server. Keeping your code between steps needs a new feature, and network tests still need to be checked in Anneal's test runner.

A bounded MPMC channel with disconnect

Part 2 of 15, about 60 minutes

Build channel(cap): a bounded queue split into a cloneable Sender and a cloneable Receiver, like a std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel that also allows several consumers.

  • send waits while full. recv waits while empty.
  • When every Sender is dropped, recv still delivers what was queued, then returns Err(RecvError); a recv that is already blocked must wake up and fail. try_recv reports Empty vs Disconnected.
  • When every Receiver is dropped, send returns Err(SendError(value)) (even one that was blocked on a full channel), and try_send returns Disconnected(value); Full(value) if merely full.
  • recv_timeout waits at most the given time in total. Receiver is an Iterator that ends on disconnect.
